source_documents.title: Experimental Photophysical investigation of a new Benzodithiophene–Diisophthalate ester revealing HLCT behavior

reference_evidence_units.quote: Steady-state and time-resolved photoluminescence studies reveal a tunable excited-state behavior that evolves systematically from local excited (LE) → hybridized local and charge transfer (HLCT) → charge-transfer (CT) character with increasing solvent polarity.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BDT-diISO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emissive state changes from LE to HLCT to CT with polarity.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, highly polar environments promote a CT-dominated state featuring markedly quenched fluorescence (ΦPL ~ 0.03), a large Stokes shift (~112 nm), broad emission (FWHM ~95 nm), and moderate intramolecular charge separation
reference_evidence_units.subject: BDT-diISO
reference_evidence_units.statement: CT-dominated emission is weak and broad.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Lip pert–Mataga analysis indicates an increase in dipole-moment from 0.3 D (S0) to 12.3 D (S1), confirming CT contribution.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BDT-diISO

reference_evidence_units.quote: Consistent with HLCT behavior, the radiative rate (kr ≈ 0.8–1.3 × 108 s− 1) remains nearly constant across solvents, reflecting the pre served LE oscillator strength, whereas the non-radiative rate (knr) in creases by more than an order of magnitude in polar environments.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BDT-diISO
reference_evidence_units.statement: kr constant, knr up >10x: the Φ drop is a non-radiative effect while LE character keeps kr.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Biexponential decay analysis further reveals solvent-dependent LE/CT mixing
reference_evidence_units.subject: BDT-diISO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Two components report the LE/CT balance.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In low-to-medium polarity media, the molecule displays LE-dominant HLCT behavior with long lifetimes (τavg ≈ 4.0 ns), small Stokes shifts, and high radiative efficiency.
reference_evidence_units.subject: BDT-diISO

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Polarity drives the emissive state toward CT (Lippert-Mataga dipole 12.3 D), which quenches emission.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The paper explains the emission efficiency by the LE/CT balance: kr stays constant through the preserved LE oscillator strength while knr rises >10x in polar solvents.
